Figure 2: Representative timeline of remote-sensing multimodal large language models (RS-MLLMs) and related works. Different colors denote the dominant technical focus of each work: Core RS-MLLM refers to general-purpose RS multimodal models covering captioning, VQA, chat, and instruction tuning; Multi-sensor highlights models designed for multi-sensor or cross-modal RS inputs, such as optical, SAR, infrared, and multi-source Earth observation data; Trust/Honesty denotes works focusing on reliability, honesty, refusal ability, and hallucination mitigation; Reasoning/RL represents methods emphasizing geospatial reasoning, chain-of-thought reasoning, or reinforcement learning-based tuning such as GRPO; Grounding/UHR indicates models targeting visual grounding, evidence grounding, ultra-high-resolution imagery, and active crop/zoom perception; Scale/Tasks denotes works emphasizing large-scale data, broad task coverage, or scale-aware modeling. Gray nodes indicate related RS foundation models or vision-language models that provide contextual background but are not treated as the main instruction-following RS-MLLM line. The lower axis summarizes the development of AI-agent research in the remote-sensing domain.
